business_scope.primary_industry_name: Serialized Digital Web Fiction and Interactive Reading App

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate registry distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage, heavily harmonized with EU directives and CJEU jurisprudence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital for EU/EEA investors)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Convention (1996, entered into force 2000, amended by 2009 and 2023 protocols)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, entered into force 2014)
Luxembourg–Japan Double Taxation Convention (2013, applicable from 2014)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Convention (1958, as amended by successive protocols through 2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as consolidated and amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant le Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as subsequently amended to comply with ECJ C-37/20 and C-601/20; Règlement CSSF n° 12-02 du 14 décembre 2012 sur la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (current consolidated version); Loi modifiée du 11 février 2018 relative au contrat de société, amending the Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (SCSp statutory source); Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre du commerce et des sociétés. Supervisory authorities: CSSF (AML/CFT), CRF/FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier), and LBR (RCS/RBE registry operator).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (RBE public layer accessible only after legitimate-interest authentication post-ECJ C-37/20; full UBO records restricted to CSSF, CRF, and obliged entities performing statutory customer due diligence)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of founder's passport (all authorized representatives and UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention states) or Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility invoice or regulated bank statement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated credit institution in the founder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / criminal record extract for the general partner (associé gérant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or judicial records authority of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming identity, professional standing and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated credit institution maintaining the founder's primary banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, where the bank refuses apostille, Consular Legalization with bank attestation translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified curriculum vitae and professional background statement of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, the general partner and each UBO against: PEP definitions under EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by (EU) 2018/843 and CSSF Regulation 12-02 (including family members and known close associates); OFAC SDN list; UN and EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; and CSSF/CRF typology and risk indicators. Standard customer due diligence applies to the Low_Risk_Standard WebNovel subscription segment; simplified due diligence may be used only in the absence of any PEP or sanctions indicator; enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval are mandatory on any positive hit or unexplained source-of-funds signal.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with electronic pre-filing through MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu eJustice channel) and the LBR online portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory filings are admissible in Luxembourgish, French or German; the SCSp partnership agreement is normally lodged in French. Foreign-language corporate names must be rendered in Latin-script transliteration, and the legal-form suffix may not be translated. The chosen name must be clearly distinguishable from names already registered in the RCS and must be immediately preceded or followed by 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCScp' (per the Law of 11 February 2018 inserting Article 100-12 into the Law of 10 August 1915). Error correction note: the statutory abbreviation is 'SCSp'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (prior CSSF authorization required)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization required)
SICAV / SICAF / Fonds d'investissement / OPC (regulated collective investment terms requiring CSSF authorization)
Société Anonyme / SA / SARL / SCS / SCA / SE (exclusive statutory suffixes of other Luxembourg corporate forms)
Bourse / Exchange / Trading Platform (financial-market regulator connotations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal, RCS issues a formal reasoned refusal notice. The applicant may (1) re-file a rectified denomination via MyGuichet.lu within 15 days; (2) if the refusal persists, submit a written administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) to the Ministry of Justice within one month; and (3) file a recours en annulation before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of the refusal notice, with an optional request for interim suspension. A parallel protective re-filing with an alternative denomination is recommended to prevent business interruption.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible through a licensed domiciliation agent: a professional registered office address in Luxembourg City satisfies LBR/RCS statutory seat requirements for an SCSp during incorporation and initial bank onboarding; however, the arrangement must demonstrate minimal commercial substance (manager availability, accounting records, AML procedures), and AED/FIU may disregard a pure letterbox arrangement in substance-over-form reviews.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 3% per annum) for a license-free, low-risk webnovel subscription platform; unannounced physical inspections are primarily directed at domiciliation agents and VAT/AED files; probability escalates if FIU reports suspicious transactions or if the platform expands into regulated payment issuance.

Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and UBO piercing assessment memorandum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariffs and prevailing translation market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark at EUR 85–120 per month

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, notably Articles 101-1 to 101-8 concerning the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013; amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS); RESA publication rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – MyLBR e-filing portal; Guichet.lu for related formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution / RCS incorporation statement filed electronically via MyLBR, followed by publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. An SCSp has no minimum capital requirement, and the amount and form of contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement. No escrow or paid-in capital deposit is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The undersigned general partner and initial limited partner adopt the SCSp partnership agreement in its present form, and each subscribed capital contribution is accepted and recorded in the capital table. (2) The registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, until changed by the general partner. (3) [Name] is appointed as managing partner/manager, with authority to execute banking, RCS, tax, and digital platform agreements. (4) The manager is authorised to file the registration application with the Luxembourg Business Registers, approve the RESA publication, obtain the Luxembourg VAT number, and take all necessary measures to commence the webnovel subscription platform. (5) All actions taken by the manager in relation to these matters are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and partnership agreement drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online name search; external civil-law notary or legal counsel (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check proposed name uniqueness using the LBR database. Confirm that the name contains 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. Draft the partnership agreement in English or French, with a French version or French legal extraction for RCS filing, specifying the general and limited partners, contributions, registered office, governing law, and the object of digital webnovel serial publishing.
required_dossiers: Identity documents/passports of general and limited partners
Power of attorney if partners act through representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged, submit three alternative names and amend the draft agreement accordingly before formal execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners acting privately or before a Luxembourg notary; notarial form is required for real-estate contributions or when securities formalities so require
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Parties sign the final SCSp partnership agreement and the capital subscription schedule. Authenticate identities and verify authority of signing representatives. Record the appointed general partner/manager and the Luxembourg registered office address.
required_dossiers: Registered office address proof (lease or landlord confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a partner identifies a formal defect, execute an addendum or restated partnership agreement before filing; notarial fees may be adjusted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg; MyLBR e-filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration application electronically, attaching the executed partnership agreement, proof of registered office, identification documents, declaration of manager acceptance, and payment confirmation of the filing fee. Obtain the temporary RCS number and filing receipt.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg
Identity documents of general and limited partners
Declaration of acceptance by the appointed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query or information request, respond within 15 calendar days with corrected or supplementary documentation; if registration is rejected, resubmit after curing the formal defect and pay any revised fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS publication service – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically arranges publication of the SCSp formation in RESA. Verify the published excerpt, the legal effective date, and obtain the final RCS extract/certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Filing receipt and approved corporate deed
Certified copy of the signed partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains errors or omissions, file a rectification request with LBR, provide the corrected text, and confirm publication of the rectification notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security and operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number applicable to digital subscription services. Register with the CCSS for any employees or for the managing partner if subject to social security. Set up payroll, accounting and tax-filing arrangements for the SCSp.
required_dossiers: VAT application form and entity details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT or CCSS requests clarification or additional proof, respond through the online portals within 15 days; amend the application, re-submit, and track the new reference number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Digital activity declaration and data protection readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie; Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD) for GDPR matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the webnovel platform requires no sectoral industrial or environmental license. Complete GDPR compliance framework for reader data, including privacy notice, records of processing, and data processor agreements with app stores/payment providers. Prepare platform terms of use, refund policy, and age-rating compliance for Apple App Store and Google Play.
required_dossiers: Activity description and ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 justification
GDPR compliance records and privacy policy
Data processing register and DPO appointment if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CNPD requests additional data-processing information, update the processing register and submit the requested documentation within the legally prescribed response period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing establishment is involved in a webnovel subscription platform
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — web serial digital publishing is not a licensed activity class in Luxembourg

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Administration) — record-only reference
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure digital service with no physical discharge; no EIA or environmental registration required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC or harmful emissions generated. Compliance is limited to general office e-waste rules, packaging rules for negligible physical goods, if any, and applicable data-centre energy-efficiency standards where servers are leased.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a remote digital platform. If an office is leased, it must meet the Luxembourg Labor Code workplace safety requirements and basic fire-safety standards applicable to commercial office use; no industrial civil-defense clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; registration and filings via MyGuichet.lu (https://myguichet.lu) and the eTVA portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the SCSp by notarial deed and register with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers portal (eJustice). 2) Obtain the 13-digit RCS number (matricule) which serves as the company TIN. 3) If a foreign entity established outside Luxembourg, register for VAT with the AEDT by filing Form 1 (or Form 645 for non-established businesses) before commencing taxable activities; a VAT number (LU + 8 digits) is issued. 4) For non-EU entities, appoint a local VAT agent in Luxembourg. 5) Where direct tax obligations arise (e.g., due to a permanent establishment), file a separate ACD TIN application. Registration must occur within 15 days before the first transaction; no minimum capital requirement for SCSp.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is statutorily tax-transparent; no domestic check-the-box election exists. Luxembourg's ATAD anti-hybrid rules may override treatment where mismatches arise. A foreign classification election (e.g., US LLC check-the-box) has no direct domestic effect; the partnership remains transparent unless an actual entity-level tax is borne abroad.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excluding VAT) for the small business exemption; for Luxembourg-established companies registration is mandatory from the first taxable supply unless the exemption applies. Non-established digital suppliers must register under the OSS when intra-EU B2C distance sales exceed EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national certification/clearance of e-invoices in Luxembourg; B2B-bilateral e-invoicing is permitted. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via PEPPOL. VAT returns and listings (e.g., Form 5, VIES) must be filed electronically through the eTVA application on MyGuichet.lu. Digital archiving of invoices is required for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT where transport is initiated/terminated in Luxembourg and is evidenced. Electronically supplied services (webnovel subscriptions) sold to non-EU business recipients are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT; sales to non-EU consumers are also outside Luxembourg VAT if the effective use/consumption occurs outside Luxembourg. Intra-EU B2B digital exports may be taxable at the customer's VAT number with no Luxembourg VAT (supply under reverse charge).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (only for physical taxation of tangible goods; not applicable to pure digital serial platform)
Bill of lading / airway bill (for physical incidental exports)
Inward remittance certificate or bank FX receipt
Subscriber registration log with IP geolocation and billing address proving non-Luxembourg destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective audit period of 6 years (general statute of limitations) from the year the VAT return was filed. Where export zero-rating is improperly claimed, AEDT will additionally assess VAT at 16% on the previously zero-rated amount, plus late interest (0.6% per annum, capitalised), and an administrative fine of 10% if the VAT is not reported or is understated; serious fraud attracts criminal penalties, including up to 5 years' imprisonment and/or a fine under Article 895 of the General Tax Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and AML market-conduct supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberalised euro-area jurisdiction under Article 63 TFEU. The euro is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account operations. There is no exchange-control approval requirement, no restriction on inward or outward payment flows, and no impediment to profit or partnership distribution remittance by an SCSp to non-resident partners. The SCSp, as a transparent partnership, may receive and disburse EUR or foreign currency without central-bank consent, subject only to BCL statistical reporting obligations arising from Regulation (EU) 2015/534 and to CSSF AML/KYC requirements imposed on the banking counterparty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export and digital-service receipts, including App Store/Google Play payouts and subscription royalties, may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency, freely reinvested, or converted at commercial market rates without requirement to sell foreign currency to the BCL or the domestic banking system.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU/EEA-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 or licensed by the CSSF; Low for offshore non-EEA digital EMIs. Legal constraints: a non-bank EMI cannot accept deposits or provide full treasury services; it can only safeguard e-money funds. For this WebNovel platform, an EU-licensed EMI could support operational collection of subscription and app-store payouts, but a Luxembourg commercial bank remains the appropriate clearing and escrow counterparty. Offshore EMIs without a Luxembourg passport are generally not viable because they lack the local establishment and supervisory co-operation required by CSSF AML rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not impose a blanket statutory requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch. Remote account opening is permitted under a CSSF-compliant risk-based approach using eIDAS-compliant e-identification, certified passport copies, apostilled corporate documents, and secure video-KYC interviews. In practice, the General Partner and the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp should expect at least one physical or video onboarding meeting, a Luxembourg registered-office verification, and submission of the notarised or certified partnership agreement, RBE extract, LEI certificate, CRS/FATCA self-certifications, and source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through SCSp with no minimum capital and limited Luxembourg substance, coupled with non-resident General Partner or non-resident UBOs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SCSp limited partnership agreement; Luxembourg RCS and RBE filings; LEI certificate; substance dossier evidencing registered office, local bank account, strategic management decisions, outsourced service provider agreements, board minutes, operational budgets, and tax classification documentation substantiating the business rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital WebNovel subscription revenue collected through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, resulting in third-party processor payouts rather than direct customer-to-SCSp wire credits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program and Google Play agreements; monthly payout statements; reconciliation reports mapping net proceeds to the SCSp operational account; in-app content licensing and distribution contracts; clear transaction-flow diagrams identifying the app stores as payment collectors only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and management chain involving multiple non-EU jurisdictions or complex trust structures, raising ultimate-beneficial-owner identification concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration and RBE filing; certified passports and proof of residential address; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation; organisational charts; notarised and apostilled power-of-attorney/trust deeds; third-party corporate registry extracts for each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injections and subsequent royalty/manufacturing disbursements to non-EEA counterparties, potentially triggering sanctions, tax-evasion, or trade-money-laundering screening alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts and invoices; webnovel catalog and IP-chain ownership documentation; evidence of real economic activity including content-development payroll and platform maintenance costs; bank-account statement history; sanctions-screening results; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; and, where relevant, a Luxembourg or European tax-law explanation of the SCSp transparent structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For euro-denominated partner contributions within the EU/EEA, use a SEPA Credit Transfer with an ISO 20022 pain.001 payment instruction and, where requested by the bank, purpose code CAPI (capital payments). For non-EUR or non-EEA injections, use a SWIFT MT103 with full remitter details, the SCSp account as beneficiary, and clear remittance information stating: capital contribution, SCSp legal name, and underlying transaction reference. Luxembourg does not require a statutory purpose code, but the bank will require an internal source-of-funds declaration, partnership deed excerpts, UBO confirmation, CRS/FATCA classification as a Passive Non-Financial Entity or equivalent, and sanctions/embargo screening. No BCL exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro payments to EU/EEA vendors, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer using pain.001/camt.056 messages. For non-euro and extra-EEA trade settlements, use SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary IBAN/account number, BIC/SWIFT, and exact remittance reference; MT202 cover is available for high-value interbank covering transactions. For platform content licensing, translation services, or production of webnovel series, documentary collections or Commercial Letters of Credit can be arranged, with the Luxembourg bank issuing an MT700 LC and settling against compliant presentation of invoices, transport/warehouse documents or digital delivery confirmation. Every outbound transaction is subject to CSSF AML controls, sanctions screening, FATCA/CRS classification, and Luxembourg VAT or reverse-charge treatment, but approval of the BCL is not required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD forward contracts and rolling FX forwards with credit lines governed by ISDA or local Luxembourg master agreements.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for less-liquid or restricted currencies used by non-EU app-store payouts when delivery in the relevant currency is impossible or uneconomical.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) to align net subscription receipts with operating expenses, royalty payments, and partner distributions while managing interest-rate mismatches.
Vanilla FX options for downside protection on major USD/EUR, GBP/EUR, or JPY/EUR conversion exposures, subject to bank credit limits and IFRS 9 hedge-accounting documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation (RBE - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - electronic RBE portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the annual anniversary of the RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 12,500; criminal fine up to EUR 1,250,000 and/or imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years for directors; temporary suspension of profit distributions until compliance is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Comptes Annuels) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of each financial year-end (31 December for calendar-year SCSp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fine of EUR 750-25,000 under the Law of 19 December 2002; repeated non-filing triggers administrative strike-off proceedings and dissolution of the SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Informational Income Tax Return (Form 300/301 - Partnership Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the following tax year; extended to 31 March of the subsequent year when filed electronically via an approved accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax (minimum EUR 150); default interest at 0.6% per month; criminal fine up to EUR 25,000 for willful omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly Form 15 due on the 15th day of the month following each calendar quarter; annual Form 14 due on 1 May; monthly filing required if taxable turnover exceeds EUR 2 million
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 500-25,000; penalty up to 10% of VAT due; late interest at 0.6% per month; criminal sanctions for VAT fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CRS/FATCA Reporting (including NIL return if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - CRS/FATCA online portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June of the year following the reporting period; NIL filing required when the SCSp is dormant or holds no reportable accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines between EUR 5,000 and EUR 250,000 depending on severity; imprisonment up to 5 years for deliberate non-compliance; freezing of assets in aggravated cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit by a cabinet de révision agréé is mandatory if the SCSp exceeds two of the three following thresholds at balance-sheet date: total assets exceeding EUR 4.4 million; net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million; average headcount exceeding 50 employees. Below these thresholds, the partners may unanimously exempt the SCSp from the appointment of an auditor and from filing annual accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the annual accounts of undertakings (as amended by the Law of 23 September 2020); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts and for listed statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file the annual UBO confirmation within one month after the annual anniversary of its RCS registration. Any transfer of partnership interests or any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within one month of the relevant event on the LBR RBE portal; supporting transaction documents and updated organizational chart must be attached. Non-confirmation triggers the penalties set out above and temporarily blocks distributions to partners until the register is complete.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (electronic RBE register maintained through LBR)
Partners' register and register of partnership-interest transfers (convention de copropriété annexes)
Minute book of partners' meetings and written resolutions
Commercial accounting records, invoices, contracts and vouchers (Article 14 of the Luxembourg Commercial Code)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,300 - 4,900 (EUR 1,200 - 4,500 per year for domiciliation with a Luxembourg société d'établissement or corporate agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,400 - 13,200 (EUR 4,000 - 12,000 per year for a statutorily audited SCSp engaged via a cabinet de révision agréé)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City composite corporate income tax rate: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax; municipal rate varies by commune up to 10.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: An SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax; profits are taxed directly in the hands of partners. A Luxembourg-resident corporate partner can benefit from the 80% net IP income exemption for qualifying copyrights and software, the 100% participation exemption on qualifying shareholdings, the notional interest deduction on new equity, and preferential taxation of income from genuine Luxembourg commercial substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Formulaire 100 - Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and Form 110 (Formulaire 110 - Déclaration pour l'impôt commercial communal) for Luxembourg-resident corporate partners or any Luxembourg permanent establishment; filed electronically through the MyGuichet.lu professional portal with Luxtrust authentication.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return must be filed by 31 May of the following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within five months after the accounting year-end. The Luxembourg tax administration may grant extensions until 31 December of the relevant year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax number, and tax status of the partner or permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filing partners must include their foreign tax identification number, country code, and treaty residence status even when only Luxembourg-source income is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and applicable basis period. The fiscal year of the webnovel platform must correspond to the audited SCSp financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the Luxembourg filing period with the SCSp's partnership accounts; do not mix foreign fiscal-year income into the Luxembourg attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result before adjustments: webnovel subscription revenue, in-app purchase commissions retained, advertising income, licensing fees, and ancillary digital sales less allowable expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-source real/IP exploitation is included; foreign income is excluded unless attributed to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments and deductions: add back non-deductible excessive management fees and artificial royalty payments; deduct qualifying IP box relief, participation exemption, and notional interest deduction amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the TP documentation annex and arm's length benchmarking if related-party transactions exceed the filing thresholds; treaty relief claims require a current Tax Residence Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or loss after carryforward and tax credits. For a tax-transparent SCSp, this box reports the partner's allocable share of Luxembourg taxable result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not offset the SCSp loss against non-Luxembourg income unless the applicable DTA permits; non-residents should treat loss carryforward strictly under Luxembourg source taxation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is subject to administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 and mandatory monthly default interest of 0.8% on unpaid tax. Filing after a formal notice may trigger an additional 10% penalty on assessed tax. Intentional fraudulent understatement exposes the taxpayer to an assessment of up to 50% of evaded tax plus criminal fines and imprisonment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SCSp fiscal transparency annex and annual allocative declaration (Partnership Annex to Form 100 / déclaration récapitulative transparente) filed through MyGuichet.lu by the general partner. A non-resident partner without a Luxembourg PE may have no separate Luxembourg CIT return, but the annex remains the official reporting instrument for profit allocations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The transparency annex must be filed by 31 May following the fiscal year-end or within five months of the accounting year-end, even if the SCSp itself has no taxable corporate result.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the general partner and all limited partners, including legal names, RCS or foreign registry numbers, country of tax residence, profit-sharing ratios, and Luxembourg tax numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners must provide their foreign tax ID and expressly state whether they are tax residents of a DTA jurisdiction; absence of a TRC may trigger treaty denial.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B - Profit and loss allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net taxable result, capital gains, deductible expenses, and any Luxembourg-source income among partners in accordance with the SCSp agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the SCSp agreement and Luxembourg transparent-partnership rules; non-residents include only Luxembourg-source or PE-attributed items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C - Withholding tax, credits, and treaty relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of any Luxembourg dividend, interest, or royalty withholding tax borne, tax credits used, and treaty benefits claimed at partner level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the original Tax Residence Certificate and cite the specific DTA article; transparent profits allocated to partners are generally not treated as Luxembourg-sourced dividends absent recharacterisation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the transparency annex triggers the same administrative fine regime as Form 100, up to EUR 25,000, plus estimated assessments against resident corporate partners, monthly default interest, and in aggravated cases criminal penalties for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a Luxembourg resident company; however, a transparent SCSp does not pay dividends, and profit allocations to partners are not subject to Luxembourg dividend WHT. If the SCSp is recharacterised as taxable, distributions become constructive dividends at 15%, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable DTA where the partner holds at least 10% for 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the partner must be the beneficial owner and tax resident of the treaty country, must not be a shell, and must supply an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued for the relevant tax year. The paying agent must receive the completed Luxembourg withholding tax relief form before payment if a reduced rate is to be applied at source; alternatively, the partner may file a refund claim with the Luxembourg direct tax administration within the statutory refund period. The submission must include a legal entity identifier, beneficial ownership declaration, shareholding history, and the applicable DTA article. For a transparent SCSp, treaty access is assessed at partner level, not at the SCSp level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on ordinary cross-border interest and royalty payments made by a Luxembourg resident company to a non-resident corporate beneficial owner, provided the recipient has no Luxembourg permanent establishment. The EU Interest & Royalties Directive provides a 0% rate between associated companies; most Luxembourg DTAs reduce any residual dividend-type royalties to 0-10%. Payments to non-resident individual authors may carry Luxembourg source taxation only if the underlying IP is exploited through a Luxembourg PE or if domestic withholding rules for authors' income are triggered; in the corporate digital-platform context, interest and royalty outbound payments are generally WHT-exempt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR: Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions in aggregate exceed EUR 500,000 or individual service transactions exceed EUR 100,000. Master File is required for groups with consolidated net revenue of EUR 50,000,000 or more; CbC Report is triggered when the consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000. All intercompany transactions with the webnovel platform, including IP royalties, subscription platform services, app-store fee sharing, and marketing recharge, must be benchmarked on arm's length terms.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has not enacted a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime in the Gulf-Cooperation-Council sense, but the General Tax Act business-purpose doctrine, EU ATAD, and treaty anti-abuse rules functionally require economic substance. An SCSp carrying on a webnovel subscription platform must demonstrate local management, a Luxembourg bank account, a substantive corporate general partner, enforceable commercial contracts, office or server presence if relevant, and real decision-making. Absent substance, the tax administration may disregard the entity, deny treaty benefits, and attribute the platform income to the true controlling enterprise.
